messages.text: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino

metadata.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. Rob Harris Sports correspondent, Sky News Thursday 3 September 2026 20:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors. UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters. FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."

messages.text: Penalised Antonelli to help Russell at Italian GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli to help Mercedes team-mate George Russell in Monza qualifying due to engine grid penalty | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli to help Mercedes team-mate George Russell in Monza qualifying due to engine grid penalty Back-of-the-grid start for Kimi Antonelli at Monza means title leader open to helping George Russell's bid for pole in Q3 on Saturday; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 3 September 2026 17:31, UK Image: George Russell is looking to claw back some of his 59-point championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli this weekend Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty. Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season. Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind. messages.text: Antonelli: Ferrari an incredible brand but I’m happy at Mercedes

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.

Kimi Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes. The 20-year-old Italian has exceeded all expectations to lead the Drivers' Championship by 59 points after 12 rounds of just his second season in Formula 1. Antonelli's superb 2026 form has seen his popularity grow massively in Italy, creating a potential dilemma for the home fans at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix who would usually be loyal to Ferrari. messages.text: Crocombe takes second hat-trick in eight days for Sussex

metadata.summary: Sussex seamer Henry Crocombe took his second hat-trick in eight days to help condemn Essex to 177 all out having been 171-3 just 26 balls before.
metadata.content: County Championship: Henry Crocombe takes hat-tricks in successive games as 23 wickets fall in Surrey vs Yorkshire - round-up | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content County Championship: Henry Crocombe takes hat-tricks in successive games as 23 wickets fall in Surrey vs Yorkshire - round-up Henry Crocombe takes second hat-trick in as many games for Sussex; Yorkshire and Surrey trade blows with the ball in action-packed day two that sees 23 wickets fall; Ben Stokes takes 3-40 but is bowled by wonder delivery from Yuzvendra Chahal Thursday 3 September 2026 19:49, UK Image: Sussex's Crocombe notched his third five-wicket haul of the season Sussex seamer Henry Crocombe took his second hat-trick in eight days to help condemn Essex to 177 all out having been 171-3 just 26 balls before. His sensational outing marked his third five-wicket haul in the County Championship this campaign, and just his second professional hat-trick after his first came against Somerset's tail in his side's last County Championship game. Crocombe - who is set to sign for Surrey at the end of the season - finished the innings with an impressive 5-39, leaving his side with a first-innings lead of 102, which was extended to 188 by the end of play with Sussex 90-4 on day two. messages.text: Hamilton reveals hope of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP Lewis Hamilton is seeking his first Ferrari victory in Italy this weekend in Monza; Hamilton is hopeful a Ferrari engine upgrade will boost his chances; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 3 September 2026 16:07, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number. Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix. The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining. Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.
